answer: The wander test I would run is Clockmaker dial standard stamped by the assay office: each dial is a calibration record countersigned by the assay office, so a farm must build a hundred real clocks by hand, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the karst of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head. The river is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
